Subject: Requesting commercial for annuity / phased onramp

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked promising. Procurement asked me to capture a commercial that matches our internal cash planning: we prefer an annuity-style payment (quarterly) over a 2-year term rather than a big upfront prepay.

We also need a phased GPU commit: we will start at 30% of the target A100-equivalent pool in Q1 of year 1, ramp to 60% in Q3, and hit 100% by Q1 of year 2. We want the price to reflect that phased commit — specifically:
- Term discount for 2-year commitment (vs month-to-month).
- Treatment of unused committed capacity during year 1 (credit or true-up?).
- Option to accelerate ramp with a 30-day notice without penalty.

Can you share a concise commercial (price, commitment schedule, payment cadence, SOW) we can circulate to finance and procurement? I attached the RFP for context.

Best,
Samira

Summary (attached PDF: RI_Proposal_Annuity_Phased_Onramp_v2.pdf)
- Term: 24 months (annuity, quarterly invoicing).
- Commit: Equivalent of 100 A100 GPUs over the term (committed capacity measured as A100-equivalent monthly units).

Attachments: full SOW and a short appendix that maps workload buckets to suggested quantization/instance mixes.

Steph — quick technical notes on credits and burst behavior:
- We can map the committed A100-equivalent units to Dedicated GPU pool reservations. Unused committed capacity becomes a credit bucket that can be consumed by on-demand bursts up to 150% of the committed baseline in any single month, subject to overall pool availability.
- Credit carry-forward: credits expire after 6 months from issuance unless used for a capacity acceleration request (where we convert to prorated consumption).
- Acceleration: 30-day notice works; if they accelerate more than +25% above current quarter baseline we cap at a one-time uplift equivalent to 10% of that quarter's invoice to cover re-provisioning.

If Sales wants to be more generous on credits or waive the 10% uplift, speak to Lauren for the commercial concession.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Derek / Samira — thanks, and appreciate the clear asks. We've aligned internally and here's the final commercial we can commit to:

Key commercial updates
- Discount: 21% off list on annualized committed spend (applies for the full 24-month term).
- Payment cadence: Quarterly annuity invoicing (net 30).
- Ramp schedule (committed): Q1 yr1 = 30%; Q3 yr1 = 60%; Q1 yr2 = 100%.
- Unused capacity treatment: annual true-up at the end of each 12-month period (no credit expiry). True-up means unused committed units will be carried as a balance and either applied as credit or refunded as a billable true-up to reconcile real consumption; refund is capped to prevent arbitrage (details in SOW).
- Acceleration: 30-day notice for ramp acceleration. For acceleration >25% in a quarter, a one-time provisioning uplift of 7.5% (reduced from 10%) will apply.

I attached an updated signable SOW (SOW_EdgeScale_Q4_signable.pdf) and a single-page commercial summary. DocuSign link here: https://docusign.com/sign/abcd-1234

If that looks good I'll route the contract for signature and ask legal to include the annual true-up language.

Best,
—Stephanie Nguyen
